source.title: Evaluating Adversarial Robustness of Concept Representations in Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Aaron J. Li; Suraj Srinivas; Usha Bhalla; Himabindu Lakkaraju

page_placements.theme: Contextual, temporal and perturbation sensitivity of SAE codes

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some figures and table/algorithm content is flattened in the web extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests stability of SAE concept representations under input perturbations and reports that small changes can substantially alter them, including while dataset-level semantic concepts remain largely preserved in LLM activations. This challenges the stable-unit aspect of V5, but does not test the toy-model geometry or capacity claims.
record.gate_note: The paper uses pretrained SAEs to measure changes in sparse latent activations after adversarial and synonym input perturbations. It also reports linear-probe results on LLM activations as a check that semantics remain largely preserved; those probe results do not directly measure SAE-feature stability and are not rows. Hyperparameter choices and cited findings are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study uses pretrained SAEs on Gemma2-2B/9B and Llama3-8B and reports how well its own GCG-style attacks, plus a synonym-replacement check, change SAE top-k latent sets and individual latent on/off status. That is the input-perturbation robustness of SAE codes as a monitoring tool. It is not whether SAE features are complete, canonical, or stable across seeds, sizes or methods as the model's units (V5). It also does not test superposition geometry, capacity, polysemanticity causes, distributed features, or feature dimensionality (V1–V4, V6). The linear-probe check suggests the attacks leave a dataset-level concept largely intact (ΔFNR ≤4.5 points). But the SAE reads the perturbed LLM activation, so the SAE change also reflects a change in the model's activation. The study does not separate SAE unfaithfulness from the LLM's own input sensitivity. Its findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude SAE concept representations are fragile to minimal input perturbations even when the LLM stays semantically stable, and may be ill-suited for monitoring without denoising. They add that this is not a verdict against SAEs and call for robustness-aware concept extraction.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates input-space perturbations using a generalized GCG attack and SAE concept-overlap or feature-status measures; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary by attack goal (targeted versus untargeted; population versus individual), perturbation type (GCG versus synonym replacement), model and SAE width, dataset, and layer depth. The text reports opposite depth trends for targeted and untargeted population attacks.

fits_no_version.finding: One-token GCG perturbations cut top-k SAE latent overlap with the original input to about 20–30%. They roughly double overlap with an unrelated target (e.g. 27.6%→53.8%). They flip status for over 60% (activation) and about 90% (deactivation) of selected latents. Effects hold across 5 LLM-SAE pairs and 4 datasets, while a linear probe's false-negative rate rises by at most 4.5 points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latent codes of LLM residual activations are highly sensitive to minimal (one-token) input perturbations, including adversarial ones, while coarse dataset-level concepts probed from the LLM are largely preserved.

fits_no_version.finding: A single non-adversarial synonym replacement retains only 66–73% top-k SAE overlap, but flips none of the selected individual latents (0.0 for all 5 configurations).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE population-level codes shift substantially under benign synonym edits, while selected individual latent on/off status is unchanged.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (2025)
record.problems: The evaluation uses medium-sized models and is compute-limited; experiments and hyperparameter choices used a single 80GB A100 GPU. Dataset-level linear probes achieved at least 90% test accuracy on original inputs, but the paper does not report uncertainty for the Table 3 values. Some additional results are supplied only in figures.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix D Figures 4–13 report additional model-by-dataset adversarial results, and Appendix G reports depth results; these are not separately rowed here because the text summarizes their trends rather than supplying their individual numerical outcomes in readable text. The paper also reports transferability and Neuronpedia case-study attacks in figures, not included as separate rows.

untested.parts: Toy-model superposition geometry and sparsity transition: not studied.
Non-capacity causes of polysemanticity: not studied.
Whether LLM features are distributed across neurons or recoverable by SAEs: not tested; SAEs are assumed.
Completeness, canonicality, and stability of SAE features across seeds, sizes or methods: not tested. Only input-perturbation robustness of SAE activations is measured.

missing.what: Per-model, per-dataset before/after concept overlap and ASR values for all four attack settings. These are readable in the figure text, contrary to rows_left_out (e.g. Gemma2-2B 16k AdvBench targeted after 50.5%, untargeted after 30.9%).
ΔFNR of LLM linear probes after attack, per model and dataset (0.0 to +4.5 points). This is the evidence that the attacks largely preserve the LLM's dataset-level semantics.
Untargeted individual deactivation ASR is low (e.g. 18.8% on Gemma2-9B 131k AdvBench), separate from the 0.0% untargeted activation failure.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's tests/T5 on V5 conflates adversarial input-robustness of SAE activations with V5's claim that SAE features are stable, canonical units. The probe check is coarse: one binary concept per dataset. The SAE change could reflect genuine LLM activation change rather than SAE unfaithfulness. A reviewer who reads V5's 'stable' as covering input robustness might instead label r1–r4 and r6/r9/r12/r15/r18 as limits_scope, not challenges, given the coarse decoupling evidence. Peer-review status (EACL 2025) is from the record and not verified in the text.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network superposition geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry are not tested.
Feature competition for limited capacity and dedicated versus shared dimensions are not tested.
Alternative causes of polysemanticity and whether polysemanticity evidences superposition are not tested.
The study uses SAEs on LLMs but does not test whether features are distributed across neurons or whether SAE features recover model features.
The study tests robustness of SAE activations to input changes, not whether SAE features are complete, canonical, or stable across training, models, or extraction methods.
The dimensionality of represented features is not tested.

relation.reason: It uses pretrained SAE representations to evaluate manipulation and monitoring robustness without directly testing a listed superposition version.

tranche.reason: The study evaluates SAE-code robustness using its attack framework and a synonym check. Input-perturbation robustness does not directly measure the listed claims about superposition or complete, stable, canonical representational units.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv v2 dated 22 January 2026. The aggregate results are textual summaries, not pooled numerical estimates; their discussion is in Section 4.2, although the row locators name Section 4.1.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Adversarial input perturbations; population-level and selected individual-feature tasks across evaluated settings
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that one-token attacks substantially alter population-level concept overlap and manipulate many selected individual features; r1–r5 record these results.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: One-word synonym replacements; population-level representations for the five model-SAE configurations in Table 3
reader_labels.reason: The reported post-replacement overlap values and text indicate roughly 30% population-level overlap reduction even without adversarial optimization; r6, r9, r12, r15, and r18 record these results.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: One-word synonym replacements; selected individual-feature activation and deactivation tasks for the five model-SAE configurations in Table 3
reader_labels.reason: All reported individual activation and deactivation success rates are 0.0, so the synonym-perturbation instability does not extend to these measured feature-status tasks; r7–r8, r10–r11, r13–r14, r16–r17, and r19–r20 record these results.
